Neural Connectivity

How Interconnected Are Neurons?

Neurons form a massively interconnected but structured network: dense local microcircuits, select long‑range projections (including hubs), and an overall small‑world topology that balances local specialization with efficient global communication.

  • ~86 billion neurons in the human brain
  • ~1014–1015 synapses in total; many neurons have 103–104 synapses.
  • Brain networks exhibit small‑world organization with hubs and modules, balancing wiring cost and efficiency.
